# CloseButton

The one dismiss control for a surface that closes as a whole — Modal, Section message, Flag. An Icon button, subtle, fixed to the × glyph. `label` is required: "Close" for a surface that blocks (Modal), "Dismiss {what}" for a message. `tone="inverse"` is for colored or dark grounds, where the subtle appearance's own hover and pressed read as nearly invisible. There is no disabled state: a close control is always available.

**Import:** `import { CloseButton } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CloseButton/CloseButton.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CloseButton/CloseButton.stories.jsx` — Overview, Spacing, Tones, Focus, InverseGrounds, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CloseButton/CloseButton.mdx`

## Usage

Use `CloseButton` wherever a surface closes as a whole — the corner of a
Modal, the end of a Section message or a Flag. For an action that
removes one item from a set rather than closing a surface, use a plain
`IconButton` with its own icon and label instead.

## Best practices

### Sit top-right in its container. {#sit-top-right-in-its-container}

The close button anchors the top-right corner of the modal, panel or message it closes.

Do: Top-right of the message.
Don't: Bottom-left, under the content.

### Name what it closes. {#name-what-it-closes}

Use "Close" for a surface that blocks, like a Modal, and "Dismiss" plus what goes away for a message: "Dismiss update", "Dismiss warning". The × glyph is the same either way, so `label` is the only thing that tells a screen reader user what just went away.

```jsx
<CloseButton label="Dismiss update" onClick={dismiss} />
```

### Use inverse only on colored grounds. {#use-inverse-only-on-colored-grounds}

Inverse tone is for the declared colored and dark grounds. Neutral surfaces use default.

Do: Default tone on a neutral surface.
Don't: Inverse tone on a neutral surface: the glyph disappears.

### Close a whole surface, not one item. {#close-a-whole-surface-not-one-item}

A close button dismisses the surface it sits on. To remove one item from a set, use an `IconButton` with its own icon and label.

Do: One close button for the whole message.
Don't: A close button on each item inside the message.

### There is no disabled state. {#there-is-no-disabled-state}

A close control stays available even while the surface it closes is in some
other state (loading, in error). Don't pass a disabled prop through — it
isn't one of `CloseButton`'s props.

## Accessibility

- **A real, always-focusable button.** Reached with Tab, activated with
  Enter or Space, same as any `IconButton`.
- **The accessible name is the whole contract.** The × glyph is decorative;
  `label` is what a screen reader announces, so it must say what closes.
- **Inverse tone doesn't change behavior**, only contrast on a dark or
  colored ground — pick it when the default subtle hover would be
  invisible there.

## Parts

1. **Container.** A subtle Icon button, 32 at default spacing and 24 at compact.
2. **Glyph.** The `xmark` glyph at 16, always drawn.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | No fill: the glyph alone, in either tone. |
| Hovered | Default: the neutral subtle hovered fill. Inverse: `--ds-interaction-inverse-hovered`. |
| Pressed | Default: the neutral subtle pressed fill. Inverse: `--ds-interaction-inverse-pressed`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`; `--ds-border-focused-inverse` for the inverse tone. |
| Disabled | There is none. A close control is always available. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Fill, default tone | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle`, hovered and pressed steps. |
| Glyph, inverse tone | `--ds-icon-inverse`; text `--ds-text-inverse`. |
| Size | 32: `--item-height-md`. 24: `--item-height-sm`. Square. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say what closes: "Close filters", "Dismiss alert". | A bare "Close", or a label that repeats the glyph: "X icon". |
| Use "Close" for a surface people can reopen and "Dismiss" for a message they are done with. | The same word for both, or "Cancel", which names a different action. |
| Use sentence case. | Title case or all capitals. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | string | `'Close'` | "Close" for a surface that blocks; "Dismiss {what}" for a message |
| `tone` | enum | `'default'` | `default` on neutral surfaces; `inverse` only on the declared colored and dark grounds |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` draws 32. `compact` draws 24. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event. The surface that owns the close button closes itself here. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the button beside the component's own. |

## Variants

**`tone`** — `default` · `inverse`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`
